MOVIES / SERIES

    About the historical journey

    This is a historical explorer, not a physical simulation of backward time travel. There is no experimentally established method for travelling into the past. This edition departs from 2026 and extends from Earth’s formation, approximately 4.54 billion years ago, through 2026—not an exact day. The 2026 archive may include ongoing or scheduled events. The map uses present-day countries; older names, borders, and Wikipedia coverage may differ. Boarding passes and arrival effects are fictional framing for real historical entries. Featured moments are examples, not a ranking of a country’s most important events.

    Wikipedia lookups require an internet connection and send your selected destination to Wikimedia. No accounts, analytics, or visitor data are stored by this app. Wikipedia’s coverage varies by country.

    THE TIME TRAVELLER’S CHALLENGE / FUTURE

    Prove you’re a time traveller.

    You’ve arrived. Now convince someone you came from another time.

    An imaginative packing challenge, not scientific proof. Tick items as you plan; nothing is uploaded or saved.

    In the future, an old phone or newspaper would show where your belongings came from—not establish that you travelled through time. Independent records would make the story more testable.

    About this simulation

    Time Travel Lab is an educational demonstration of special-relativity time dilation. Results assume an idealised journey at constant speed on each leg, with negligible time spent accelerating or turning around. Gravity is not modelled, and animations are illustrative. This is not a tool for real-world spacecraft navigation or mission planning.

    THE SCIENCE / NOT SCIENCE FICTION

    One universe.
    Different clocks.

    In special relativity, a clock moving relative to Earth accumulates less time than Earth’s clocks over the corresponding Earth-frame interval. The closer its speed is to light, the greater the difference.

    γ = 1 / √(1 − v²/c²)Traveller time = Earth time / γ

    Formula reference: OpenStax, University Physics Volume 3, §5.3: Time Dilation.

    The text gives Δt = γΔτ, with γ = 1/√(1 − v²/c²). Here Δt is Earth-frame elapsed time and Δτ is traveller proper time; rearranging gives Δτ = Δt/γ.

    Here, v is your speed, c is the speed of light (299,792.458 km/s), and γ is the Lorentz factor.

    This model assumes an idealised out-and-back trip at constant speed on each leg, with negligible time spent accelerating or turning around. It ignores gravity and Earth’s motion. A real mission would require accounting for those effects.

    It is forward time travel in the sense of ageing less than people on Earth. It cannot take you into the past, and an object with mass cannot reach the speed of light.
